label: Sep 7–11
intro: Sample week. Everything here is invented — a made-up class, a made-up kid, a made-up lesson plan — to show how a real week reads. School is doing weather; this is the same week folded into the evening you're already having.

gelds.text: Observes and describes the natural world

books.title: Little Cloud
books.author: Eric Carle
books.ask: "What did the little cloud turn into?" Let him name each one before you turn the page.
books.askStretch: "Why does the cloud keep changing?" He'll reach for a story reason. Take it — an explanation he invented beats one he repeated.

books.title: The Rain Came Down
books.author: David Shannon
books.ask: "Why is everybody so grumpy?" Point at one character at a time.
books.askStretch: "What changed at the end?" The weather changed and every mood changed with it — that link is the whole book, and it's a level past naming who's upset.

days.title: What's the sky doing?
days.school: At school: naming today's weather with picture cards, a class weather chart, and Little Cloud.

moves.title: Weather window
moves.do: Stand at the window and name it together — sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy. He picks the word.
moves.stretch: Ask what he'd wear outside and why. Matching clothes to weather is the reasoning step; the label on its own isn't.

moves.title: One word for the sky
moves.do: Everyone gives one word for how the sky looked today.
moves.stretch: His word can't be one somebody already used. Running out of the easy ones is exactly where vocabulary grows.

moves.title: Rain in the tub
moves.do: Pour water through a cup with holes in it and call it rain. He says the word every time.
moves.stretch: Ask where the rain was before it fell. Any answer counts — you're after the idea that the water was somewhere else first.

moves.title: Little Cloud
moves.do: Stop on each shape and let him name what the cloud turned into.
moves.stretch: Ask what HE would turn a cloud into, then have him draw it in the air with one finger.

days.title: Clouds and rain
days.school: At school: where rain comes from, cotton-ball cloud art, counting raindrops to 10.

moves.title: Cloud hunt
moves.do: Go outside and find one cloud. Say what it looks like.
moves.stretch: Find two, then say which is bigger and which is higher. Comparing two things is harder than describing one.

moves.title: The weather report
moves.do: He gives the table the weather report for today.
moves.stretch: Now tomorrow's forecast, with one reason. Being wrong is completely fine — committing to a guess is the skill.

moves.title: Float or sink
moves.do: Sort the bath toys into things that float and things that don't.
moves.stretch: He calls it before each one goes in. One guess he has to commit to is worth ten he makes afterward.

moves.title: Count the drops
moves.do: Count 10 things out loud before lights out. Point at each one.
moves.stretch: Count to 20, then start at 6 and keep going. Counting on from a number instead of restarting at 1 is the kindergarten version.

days.title: Wind
days.school: At school: what wind does, blowing paint through straws, ribbon streamers outside.

moves.title: Blow it across
moves.do: A straw and a cotton ball, raced across the table. First one to the edge.
moves.stretch: Line up three things and have him predict which will move and which won't — then test all three. He has to say why the heavy one didn't.

moves.title: What did the wind move?
moves.do: Name anything you saw moving outside today.
moves.stretch: Now something the wind can't move. Finding the edge of a rule is real thinking, and most kids his age have never been asked.

moves.title: Make waves
moves.do: Blow across the water and watch it move.
moves.stretch: A big wave, then a small one, on purpose. Then he tells you what he did differently.

moves.title: Little Cloud again
moves.do: Second read. He'll start saying the shapes before you do — let him.
moves.stretch: Cover the words and have him tell the story from the pictures. Retelling in his own words is pre-reading.

days.title: Sun and shadows
days.school: At school: sun and shadows, tracing shadows on the playground, warm and cool sorting.

moves.title: Shadow tag
moves.do: Try to step on each other's shadow. Loud and short.
moves.stretch: Ask him to make his shadow taller, then shorter. Working out that moving changes the shadow is the whole lesson, and he has to find it himself.

moves.title: Warm thing, cool thing
moves.do: One warm thing and one cool thing you each touched today.
moves.stretch: Ask which ones the sun made warm. Sorting by cause instead of by feel is the harder cut.

moves.title: Where did the light go?
moves.do: Hold a hand between the light and the water and find the dark patch.
moves.stretch: He makes the shadow bigger without moving the light. Moving the hand closer is the answer — let him hunt for it.
moves.skill: Changing one thing at a time

moves.title: Line them up
moves.do: Line up ten blocks and count 1 to 10, then back down to 1. Backwards is the hard part.
moves.stretch: He turns around, you take one away, and he says which number is missing.

days.title: The seasons turn
days.school: At school: review the week, four-seasons tree art, weather freeze dance.

moves.title: Weather freeze dance
moves.do: Play a song. When you pause it, call a weather word — he freezes as sun, rain, or wind.
moves.stretch: He runs the music and calls the words, including the ones from Wednesday. Running the game means holding the whole list in his head.

moves.title: Best weather, worst weather
moves.do: Everyone picks a favourite kind of weather and says why.
moves.stretch: He picks one somebody else would like and says why they'd pick it. Arguing for a preference that isn't his is the hard one.

moves.title: The whole week on the wall
moves.do: He draws every kind of weather from this week on the tub wall and names them. Wipe them away together — that part is half the fun.
moves.stretch: He writes the first letter under each one. R for rain, W for wind. Letters attached to something he cares about beat a worksheet.
moves.skill: Letters with a reason to exist

moves.title: He picks the book
moves.do: His choice tonight. Before you open it, ask him to tell you one thing that happens in it.
moves.stretch: After the ending, ask what happens next — a page that isn't in the book. Making up story past the last page is pre-writing.

class: Names the weather and describes the sky
Sorts warm and cool, wet and dry
Joins group discussion about what he observed
his: Says what caused the weather he's describing
Makes a prediction out loud and then checks it
Counts to 20 and back down, and counts on from a number
Explains a preference that isn't his own

weekend: At the park, ask him to find one thing the wind is moving and one thing it isn't. That's the whole assignment.

kindness.text: You held the door open for somebody carrying a lot.
You shared your umbrella when it started raining.
You splashed a puddle on purpose to get somebody wet.
Your friend lost a mitten, so you helped look for it.
You let somebody else pick the game first.
You knocked the leaf pile over while they were raking it.
You said "good morning" to somebody standing alone.
You grabbed the last cookie without asking.
You helped put the boots away without being asked.
You laughed when somebody slipped in the mud.
You waited your turn on the swing.
